# Downtown Mobility Budget Brief

The draft budget shifts operating funds from peak-hour parking enforcement<sup>[1](#footnote-1)</sup> to evening bus frequency pilots in the central corridor<sup>[2](#footnote-2)</sup>, with the stated goal of reducing wait times before winter service changes take effect.

Analysts note that the projected ridership gain depends on temporary signal-priority equipment<sup>[3](#footnote-3)</sup> and on extending the regional fare cap to municipal passes<sup>[4](#footnote-4)</sup>, neither of which is fully funded in the current ordinance.

Council staff also warned that storefront loading zones may be reduced on two blocks near the market<sup>[5](#footnote-5)</sup>, a tradeoff merchants accepted only after the city promised a six-month review<sup>[6](#footnote-6)</sup>.

1. Parking enforcement redeployment is described in the March staffing memo approved by the transportation committee.
2. The pilot covers Route 6 and Route 14 between 6 p.m. and 10 p.m. on weekdays.
3. Temporary signal-priority units are leased for nine months and require separate maintenance funding.
4. The fare-cap extension is contingent on a data-sharing agreement with the regional transit authority.
5. The affected blocks are on Alder Street between 3rd and 5th Avenue.
6. The review period begins after installation and includes monthly delivery-time observations.

issues.description: Each footnote marker in the body incorrectly includes the literal source numeral before the superscript link (e.g. `enforcement1<sup>...`), duplicating the footnote number instead of rendering a single inline footnote reference.

The inline footnote markup is malformed/noisy: `1<sup>[\[1\]](#footnote-1)</sup>` shows escaped brackets inside `<sup>` rather than clean Markdown like `<sup>[1](#footnote-1)</sup>` or standard GFM footnote syntax.
The footnote list adds backlink arrows and anchor targets not present in the intended content. While not content loss, this introduces extra output beyond the source document.
